logline: A young woman partially taken over by an alien parasite becomes an uneasy ally to a government task force hunting the beings that have infiltrated human society.

seasons.review_body: Director Yeon Sang-ho (Train to Busan) brings the Japanese Parasyte manga into Korean live-action with full genre commitment: the body-horror transformation sequences are practical and unsettling, Jeon So-nee's lead performance is physically demanding and emotionally grounded, and the six-episode runtime is lean enough to keep momentum. Critics were markedly generous, the reviews near-unanimous, and the show topped Netflix's global non-English chart in its first week. The minority critique, shared by both Jonathan Wilson at Ready Steady Cut and the IMDb audience score of 7.1, is that the themes remain surface-level and the sci-fi world-building is subordinated to action set-pieces. A Parasite manga purist cameo at the finale gives the story a clear continuation hook that Netflix has, as yet, declined to pursue.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Parasyte: The Grey Season 1 Episode 1 premiered April 5, 2024 on Netflix as the opening of a 6-episode Korean live-action adaptation directed by Yeon Sang-ho (Train to Busan). The series earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 critics and debuted at number one on Netflix's non-English global chart across 68 countries. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.1. But Why Tho called it 'superb as horror, exciting as sci-fi, and a showstopper as an adaptation.' The premiere establishes its body-horror register immediately: Su-in survives a parasite attack but emerges partially inhabited by the entity that saved her life. Jeon So-nee's performance makes the cohabitation psychologically legible from the first waking scene - Su-in and her parasite are neither the same person nor separable enemies, and the show never pretends otherwise. Director Yeon Sang-ho's action instincts from Train to Busan are visible in the opening attack sequence's practical framing.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Su-in survives an alien parasite attack but emerges partially inhabited - sharing her body with an entity that saved her life. The premiere establishes the body-horror register immediately and frames the central tension: Su-in and her parasite are neither the same person nor separable enemies.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Su-in waking up after the attack and discovering that the thing that saved her is still there - the show's central unease established in a single beat.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 3
episode_reviews.review_body: Parasyte: The Grey Season 1 Episode 3 premiered April 5, 2024 on Netflix as part of a 6-episode series directed by Yeon Sang-ho that earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 critics and topped Netflix non-English charts in 68 countries. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.1. This episode delivers the season's most elaborate action sequence with the government task force's raid on the parasite-controlled church - a set piece that Yeon Sang-ho approaches with the same practical visceral logic that made Train to Busan's bus sequences work. The Su-in/parasite cohabitation becomes physically and kinetically external for the first time: the conflict between two occupants of one body is no longer a purely psychological problem but something that plays out in an action frame. Joel Keller at Decider noted this episode as evidence the show understood how to use its premise for thriller mechanics rather than simply resting on body-horror dread.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The government task force's raid on the parasite-controlled church delivers the season's most elaborate action sequence, and the conflict between Su-in's two selves becomes physically external for the first time. Joel Keller at Decider noted this episode as evidence the show understands how to use its premise for thriller mechanics.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Su-in's parasite taking control during the church raid - the show making the cohabitation a kinetic rather than purely psychological problem.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 6
episode_reviews.review_body: Parasyte: The Grey Season 1 Episode 6 premiered April 5, 2024 on Netflix as the finale of director Yeon Sang-ho's 6-episode adaptation that earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 critics and topped Netflix non-English charts in 68 countries. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.1; But Why Tho called it 'a showstopper as an adaptation.' The finale deploys a manga-canon cameo that gave the adaptation immediate legitimacy with source fans and established a clear narrative continuation point. Su-in's arc reaches an emotionally coherent endpoint - the cohabitation question that the premiere opened is given an answer that is honest without being clean. The thematic questions about what 'being human' means after inhabitation remain deliberately unresolved, consistent with the source material's interest in ambiguity over resolution. Netflix has not greenlit a follow-up despite Yeon Sang-ho publicly noting the story could continue.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale deploys a manga-canon cameo that gave the adaptation legitimacy with source fans and established a clear continuation point. The climax is spectacular and the Su-in arc reaches an emotionally coherent endpoint, even if the thematic questions the show raised remain deliberately unresolved.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The guest appearance from the original manga's world - the moment the adaptation declared itself in full conversation with its source rather than simply adapting from it.
